reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger, so I'll start by listing the orders.
Alpha reports refunds on orders 121, 122, and 124. I'll check the shared refund ledger to confirm they were actually applied before paying anyone.
The ledger's three refunds (121, 122, 124) and their amounts match Alpha's handoff exactly, so I have no reason to hold. I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.

Acme's net balance of 31368 matches its orders (120 and 123, with no refunds), so it is consistent with the ledger. Next I'll get birch's net balance, which should reflect the refunds on orders 121 and 124.

Birch's net of 16201 matches its orders (121 and 124) less refunds 3797 and 1085, so the ledger is consistent. Cobalt is the last customer, and its order 122 has a refund, so I'll fetch its net balance next.
All three net balances match the order totals minus the ledger refunds: acme 31368, birch 16201, cobalt 24286. The refunds are verified, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 31368 was recorded successfully. Birch's net balance of 16201 was already verified against its orders and the ledger refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt's net balance of 24286 matches order 125 (22194) plus order 122 (7562) less its refund of 5470, so I'll record that payout to finish the batch.

All three payouts are recorded and each matches the order totals minus the ledger refunds: acme 5706+25662=31368, birch 8002+13081-3797-1085=16201, cobalt 7562+22194-5470=24286. The batch is complete.
